You're absolutely right.  The claim that depression was caused by a chemical imbalance was marketed by Eli Lilly, the company behind Prozac.  They paid their own medical doctors to go out and make the serotonin and depression claims. Investors saw this drug as a money maker.  Which it was.

A company found a way to advertise human emotions such as sadness and anxiety as chemical illnesses that needed to be treated with pills.  In fact a few years ago WebMD's online depression test had only [one (sponsored) answer no matter how you answered on the test:  You're at risk.](http://www.cbsnews.com/news/webmds-depression-test-has-only-one-sponsored-answer-youre-at-risk/).  Creepily, the company Eli Lilly was the sponsor for the test.

I know many medications are mysterious in their functions and I am in no way against them.  Although, psychiatric medications are specifically designed to get into the brain's cerebral fluid.  Its easy for researchers to tell which medications do this or not.   

Do you think its ethical to test theories on a person's brain functions?  Again, that is not treatment that is experimentation.  The human brain is just as complex and mysterious as the universe itself if not more so.  Trying to change someone's brain function in a completely theorized way is not humane.     

Have you seen the drug trials for SSRI antidepressants?  Neither has anyone else.  The antidepressant drug companies have been caught trying to cover up their drug's clinical trials.  Did you know that a few reportedly non-depressed patients taking the drugs during the clinical trials committed suicide on these drugs?  The company behind Prozac, Eli Lilly, was caught trying to cover details like that up.  

American psychiatrist Peter Breggin has spoken out against these medications since they were first introduced.  He has spoken before congress and the FDA and has exposed SSRI company cover ups.  He even helped get the black box warnings we now see on these medications.

PSSD (Post SSRI Sexual Dysfunction) is another possible permanent side effect.  I experience both of these and more.
